source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: Root rot, caused by the same Phytophthora palmivora pathogen responsible for stem/patch canker in durian, attacks the root system, typically starting with fine feeder roots and progressing to larger structural roots in waterlogged or poorly drained soil. Above-ground symptoms are often the first thing a grower notices -- gradual yellowing and thinning of the canopy, wilting despite adequate soil moisture elsewhere in the orchard, and reduced vigor or dieback -- by which point the root damage is often already significant, since root symptoms are hidden underground. Waterlogging, poor drainage, and soil compaction are the main predisposing conditions. General control approach: ensure good drainage is designed into the orchard from planting (raised mounds/beds in areas with a high water table, as described in Source A), avoid over-watering, and where a tree shows root-rot symptoms, improve drainage around it immediately and treat with an appropriate systemic fungicide as recommended for Phytophthora control; severely affected trees with extensive root loss may not recover and should be removed to prevent the pathogen spreading through the soil to neighboring trees.
